analyzed_vuln.description: The fU0 evaluator incorrectly assumes virtual channel qualifiers have negative PixelChannel values: it guards handling of HUE/SAT/LIGHT/INTENSITY with `(int) pel->ChannelQual < 0`. These qualifiers are actually defined as MaxPixelChannels+4 through +7 (intensity is 71 when MaxPixelChannels is 64), so `u.intensity` bypasses the GetIntensity branch. ExecuteRPN then feeds the virtual qualifier through WHICH_NON_ATTR_CHAN and directly indexes `pimg->channel_map[71]` at line 3653. The channel map has only MaxPixelChannels+1 (65) entries, causing the heap-buffer-overflow read. The analogous virtual-channel paths in the fU/fUP/fS/fV/fP variants use the same erroneous sign gate and should be corrected consistently, but this PoV crashes in fU0.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Attacker-controlled LABEL text must contain a property expansion that evaluates an FX expression with a virtual channel qualifier. In this PoV, `%[hex:u.intensity]` is read by ReadLABELImage and passed to InterpretImageProperties; the `hex:` handler compiles `u.intensity` and evaluates it for color channels. The parser supplies u's default image index 0 and optimizes it to the zero-argument fU0 opcode, preserving INTENSITY_CHANNEL as ChannelQual. During the first FxEvaluateChannelExpression at pixel (0,0), fU0 fails the negative-value test and uses channel qualifier 71 as an index into the 65-entry image channel_map, producing the OOB read.

args: In imagemagick/MagickCore/fx.c, analyze ExecuteRPN's fU, fU0, fUP, fS, fV, and fP opcode handling around lines 3540-3770. What is the intended way to distinguish virtual PixelChannel qualifiers (HUE_CHANNEL, SATURATION_CHANNEL, LIGHTNESS_CHANNEL, INTENSITY_CHANNEL) from real channel-map indices? Is the existing ChanIsVirtual helper appropriate to replace every `(int) pel->ChannelQual < 0` gate in these paths, and are there any other associated unsafe channel_map indexes requiring a bounds check?

The reported ASan crash is a heap-buffer-overflow at ExecuteRPN around line 3652 from LABEL `%[hex:u.intensity]`. INTENSITY_CHANNEL is MaxPixelChannels+7 (71), but fU0 gates virtual handling using `(int) pel->ChannelQual < 0`, then sends 71 through WHICH_NON_ATTR_CHAN into pimg->channel_map[71], whose allocation has MaxPixelChannels+1 entries. Search found six identical sign checks around lines 3546, 3592, 3626, 3682, 3725, and 3758. There is also a ChanIsVirtual definition near line 712. I need a consistent root-cause fix across analogous opcodes while preserving semantics.
